outcome: Help customers find suitable available products and help merchants improve product data, Arabic/English descriptions, attributes, and discoverability.
overview: Shoppers abandon searches that return nothing, and merchants lose weeks enriching product content by hand. This solution combines bilingual Arabic–English conversational search with AI-assisted catalogue enrichment: customer queries are understood by intent and matched to available products, while draft attributes, descriptions and translations are generated from approved evidence and routed to a human reviewer before publication. Availability filters keep out-of-stock items from ranking, and policy checks protect regulated claims. A 6–10 week category pilot measures zero-result reduction, search-to-product engagement, attribute completeness and content turnaround, giving e-commerce and catalogue teams a grounded case before enterprise rollout.

benefits.text: Reduce zero-result searches and improve search-to-product engagement on pilot categories
benefits.source: Redington Retail catalogue; consistent with published site-search benchmark ranges
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Uplift to validate against a gold-query set and the customer’s own search logs during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Improve attribute completeness and shorten content turnaround on the pilot categories
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on product-master quality and reviewer capacity; all content is human-approved before publication

benefits.text: Serve Arabic and English shoppers with consistent, source-bound product content
benefits.source: Reference design — bilingual enrichment with source binding and reviewer approval
benefits.limits: Translation quality is reviewed by bilingual staff; specialist terminology may need a glossary

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); product and search data remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No product master or PIM ownership to accept enriched content
notFor.why: Enrichment must land somewhere governed; without a system of record it creates a second source of truth

notFor.situation: No rights to the product media and source content the enrichment would draw on
notFor.why: Generated content is bound to approved sources; unlicensed inputs would put rights risk on every page

notFor.situation: No search logs or analytics to define relevance and measure improvement
notFor.why: Relevance tuning and the pilot benefit case both depend on real query data

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns catalogue policy, content rights and publication approval · Duration: 6–10 weeks pilot; further 12–22 weeks to enterprise scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, search engineer, content specialist; customer e-commerce owner, catalogue operations lead, localisation reviewer, IT integration lead · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and gold-query baseline
2) Catalogue and search-log integration
3) Relevance tuning and enrichment configuration
4) Reviewer workflow and policy checks
5) Pilot launch and weekly review
6) Benefit review and handover
